A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OmniDiff benchmark and M3Diff model. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations and dataset/module ablations in Tables 3–8, together with dataset analyses and qualitative case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical evaluations and adds controlled comparisons, backbone ablations, and LLM-based evaluation in supplementary Tables 11–13.

M1.justification: The MDP operations, multi-scale integration, and one-stage fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. The additional backbone experiments test the existing module without introducing a new algorithmic component or adaptation procedure.

E1.justification: The training datasets, benchmark coverage, and image-difference-captioning tasks are retained. The new appendix experiments reuse OmniDiff-Real, OmniDiff-Render, IEdit, and CLEVR-DC; they add model configurations and evaluation procedures rather than new data domains or tasks.

E2.justification: The original comparison tables retain their comparator sets. Supplementary Table 11 newly includes FINER-MLLM in the CLEVR-DC comparison, while Table 12 adds InternVL3-8B comparisons and fine-tuned Qwen2.5-VL controls without MDP, extending the earlier zero-shot Qwen comparison.

E3.justification: New supplementary protocols include reproducing FINER-MLLM with the same 896k training samples as M3Diff, testing MDP with Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3-8B, and scoring captions with GPT-4o on a 0–100 ground-truth-aspect-coverage rubric. These substantially expand the evaluation design; the original splits, metrics, and main-model training budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the original single-backbone ablations in Table 6, Table 12 tests whether MDP remains beneficial on two additional backbones. Table 13 evaluates training with versus without OmniDiff using semantic judgments from GPT-4o. These add substantial evidence about module portability and dataset utility; the existing qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The new appendix tables continue reporting point scores.

E6.justification: Tables 11–13 add controlled FINER-MLLM results, cross-backbone ablation results, and LLM scores; for example, OmniDiff-Real scores are 12.3 without OmniDiff training and 37.3 with it. Table 5 changes M3Diff's BLEU-4/METEOR/CIDEr/SPICE from 33.9/26.3/135.2/26.5 to 33.6/26.5/136.6/27.5, matching the already-existing Table 6 values. Table 11's FINER-MLLM scores use different training conditions from Table 3 and are additional results, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and operations in Equations 1–8 are retained. No new theorem, proof, derivation, or formal assumption is introduced; the GPT-4o scoring rubric is an evaluation-protocol addition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: the diverse, finely annotated OmniDiff dataset, the plug-and-play MDP module within M3Diff, and strong performance across IDC benchmarks. The new experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: New Section 9.2 tentatively attributes LLaVA-OneVision's competitive performance to greater use of multi-image pretraining data and discusses MDP's effectiveness across backbones. The existing OCR failure discussion and proposed extension to video remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project homepage link and supplies the complete GPT-4o evaluation prompt in Figure 6. The existing implementation details and hyperparameter table are retained. Both abstracts still describe code, data, and model release as forthcoming, so the PDFs do not establish that those resources became available.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to the LLM-as-a-judge survey and InternVL3 to support the new evaluations. The related-work narrative and research positioning remain largely unchanged; most other reference edits update metadata for already-cited works.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording corrections, including changing '324 scene pairs' to '324 scenes', and adds corresponding-author information and acknowledgements. A new supplementary Experiments section precedes the retained Case Study, renumbered from Section 9 to Section 10. The main narrative is largely preserved.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 11–13 and the evaluation-prompt Figure 6, redraws the Figure 4 word cloud, and relocates Figure 3 and Table 3. The two-column design, existing table structures, and qualitative case-study panels are retained, with localized layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: V1 did not establish matched training data for its FINER-MLLM comparison and tested MDP on only one backbone. V2's identical-data comparison and two additional backbone ablations address important gaps in comparison fairness and support for the plug-and-play claim. It also resolves the IEdit discrepancy between Tables 5 and 6. These substantially strengthen the central empirical argument, although uncertainty reporting and detailed settings for the new evaluations remain limited.
